titleEnglish: Gelin Ey Aşıklar — Come, O Lovers
note: By Yunus Emre (13th c.). Each line is followed by the invocation “Hû Mevlam Hû Hû.”

verses.ar:
Gelin ey aşıklar gelin · Hû Mevlam Hû Hû
Bu menzil uzağa benzer · Hû Mevlam Hû Hû
verses.en: Come, O lovers, come — Hû, my Lord, Hû Hû; this way-station seems far away — Hû, my Lord, Hû Hû.

verses.ar:
Nazar kıldım şu dünyaya · Hû Mevlam Hû Hû
Kurulmuş tuzağa benzer · Hû Mevlam Hû Hû
verses.en: I gazed upon this world — it seems like a snare that has been set.

verses.ar:
Bir pirin eteğin tuttum · Hû Mevlam Hû Hû
Ona beli deyip gittim · Hû Mevlam Hû Hû
verses.en: I took hold of a master's hem; I gave him my pledge and went on my way.

verses.ar:
Nice yüzbin günah ettim · Hû Mevlam Hû Hû
Herbiri bir dağa benzer · Hû Mevlam Hû Hû
verses.en: How many hundred-thousand sins I have committed — each one seems like a mountain.

verses.ar:
Ağla aşık Yunus ağla · Hû Mevlam Hû Hû
Sen özünü Hakk'a bağla · Hû Mevlam Hû Hû
verses.en: Weep, lover Yunus, weep; bind your very self to the Truth (God).

verses.ar:
Ağlar isen kendine ağla · Hû Mevlam Hû Hû
Elden vefa yoğa benzer · Hû Mevlam Hû Hû
verses.en: If you weep, weep for yourself — loyalty from others seems not to exist.

verses.ar:
Ağla aşık Yunus ağla · Hû Mevlam Hû Hû
Sen özünü Hakk'a bağla · Hû Mevlam Hû Hû
verses.en: Weep, lover Yunus, weep; bind your very self to the Truth (God).

titleEnglish: Güzel Aşık Cevrimizi — Fair Lover, Our Trial

verses.ar:
Güzel aşık cevrimizi
Çekemezsin demedim mi
Bu bir rıza lokmasıdır
Yiyemezsin demedim mi
verses.en: Fair lover, did I not tell you that you could not bear the trial we bring? This is a morsel of [divine] contentment — did I not tell you that you could not swallow it?

verses.ar:
Yemeyenler kalır naçar
Gözlerinden kanlar saçar
Bu bir demdir gelir geçer
Duyamazsın demedim mi
verses.en: Those who do not eat it are left helpless, scattering tears of blood from their eyes. This is a moment that comes and passes — did I not tell you that you could not perceive it?

verses.ar:
Bu dervişlik bir dilektir
Bilene büyük devlettir
Yensiz yakasız gömlektir
Giyemezsin demedim mi
verses.en: This dervishhood is a calling — to the one who knows it, a great fortune. It is a shirt with no sleeves and no collar — did I not tell you that you could not wear it?

verses.ar:
Çıkalım meydan yerine
Erelim Ali sırrına
Can ü başı Hak yoluna
Koyamazsın demedim mi
verses.en: Let us step out into the gathering-place and reach the secret of Ali; your life and your head upon the path of the Truth — did I not tell you that you could not lay them down?

verses.ar:
Aşıklar kara bahtı olur
Hakk'ın katında kutlu olur
Muhabbet baldan tatlı olur
Yiyemezsin demedim mi
verses.en: Lovers are of dark fortune, yet blessed in the presence of the Truth. Love is sweeter than honey — did I not tell you that you could not taste it?

verses.ar:
Pir Sultan Abdal Şahımız
Hakk'a ulaşır rahımız
On İki İmam katarımız
Uyamazsın demedim mi
verses.en: Pir Sultan Abdal is our Shah; our path reaches the Truth. The Twelve Imams are our caravan — did I not tell you that you could not keep pace with it?

titleEnglish: Yemen İllerinde Veysel Karani — Veysel Karani in the Lands of Yemen
note: By Yunus Emre (13th c.), in praise of Uways al-Qaranī, the Prophet's ﷺ devoted follower from Yemen.

verses.ar:
Hakk'ın Habibi'nin sevgili dostu
Yemen illerinde Veysel Karani
verses.en: The beloved friend of the Beloved of the Truth — Veysel Karani, in the lands of Yemen.

verses.ar:
Söylemez yalanı, yemez haramı
Yemen illerinde Veysel Karani
verses.en: He tells no lie and eats nothing forbidden — Veysel Karani, in the lands of Yemen.

verses.ar:
Seherde kalkuben yola giderdi
Hakk'ın binbir ismin zikir ederdi
Allah Allah deyu deve güderdi
Yemen illerinde Veysel Karani
verses.en: He would rise at dawn and set out on his way, calling upon the thousand-and-one names of the Truth; saying 'Allah, Allah' he would tend his camels — Veysel Karani, in the lands of Yemen.

verses.ar:
Elinde asası hurma dalından
Eğninde hırkası deve yününden
Asla hata gelmez onun dilinden
Yemen illerinde Veysel Karani
verses.en: In his hand a staff of palm-branch, on his shoulders a cloak of camel's wool; never does a wrong word come from his tongue — Veysel Karani, in the lands of Yemen.

verses.ar:
Aşık Yunus eydür ben de varaydım
Ol mübarek hub cemalin göreydim
Ayağın tozuna yüzler süreydim
Yemen illerinde Veysel Karani
verses.en: Yunus the lover says: would that I too could go, that I might behold that blessed, lovely face, and press my face into the dust of his feet — Veysel Karani, in the lands of Yemen.

titleEnglish: Şu Cennetin İrmakları — The Rivers of Paradise
note: By Yunus Emre (13th c.). Each couplet closes with the refrain “Allah deyu deyu” — “saying: Allah, Allah.”

verses.ar:
Şol cennetin ırmakları akar Allah deyu deyu
Çıkmış İslam bülbülleri öter Allah deyu deyu
verses.en: The rivers of that Paradise flow on, saying: Allah, Allah; the nightingales of Islam have risen and sing, saying: Allah, Allah.

verses.ar:
Salınır tûba dalları Kur'an okur hem dilleri
Cennet bağının gülleri kokar Allah deyu deyu
verses.en: The branches of the Tuba tree sway, and their tongues recite the Qur'an; the roses of the garden of Paradise give off their scent, saying: Allah, Allah.

verses.ar:
Kimi yiyip kimi içer hep melekler rahmet saçar
İdris nebî hûlle biçer biçer Allah deyu deyu
verses.en: Some eat and some drink, and everywhere the angels scatter mercy; the prophet Idris cuts out robes of honour, cutting, saying: Allah, Allah.

verses.ar:
Altındandır direkleri gümüştendir yaprakları
Uzandıkça budakları biter Allah deyu deyu
verses.en: Its pillars are of gold, its leaves are of silver; as its branches stretch out they bud and grow, saying: Allah, Allah.

verses.ar:
Aydan arıdır yüzleri misk-i amberdir sözleri
Cennette Huri kızları gezer Allah deyu deyu
verses.en: Their faces are purer than the moon, their words are musk and amber; the maidens of Paradise stroll about, saying: Allah, Allah.

verses.ar:
Hakka aşık olan kişi akar gözlerinin yaşı
Pür nûr olur içi dışı söyler Allah deyu deyu
verses.en: The one who loves the Truth — the tears stream from their eyes; their inward and outward being becomes full of light, saying: Allah, Allah.

verses.ar:
Ne dilersen Hak'tan dile kılavuzla gir bu yola
Bülbül aşık olmuş güle öter Allah deyu deyu
verses.en: Whatever you wish, ask it of the Truth; enter this path with a guide; the nightingale has fallen in love with the rose and sings, saying: Allah, Allah.

verses.ar:
Açıldı gökler kapısı rahmetle doldu hepisi
Sekiz cennetin kapısı açar Allah deyu deyu
verses.en: The gate of the heavens has opened, and all of them are filled with mercy; the gates of the eight Paradises open, saying: Allah, Allah.

verses.ar:
Rıdvan'durur kapı açan İdris'durur hûlle biçen
Kevser şarabını içen kanar Allah deyu deyu
verses.en: It is Ridwan who opens the gate, it is Idris who cuts the robes of honour; the one who drinks the wine of Kawthar is quenched, saying: Allah, Allah.

verses.ar:
Miskin Yunus var yârına koma bugünü yarına
Yarın Hakkın divanına varam Allah deyu deyu
verses.en: Poor Yunus, go to your Beloved; do not put off today until tomorrow; tomorrow I shall come before the court of the Truth, saying: Allah, Allah.

titleEnglish: Sordum Sarı Çiçeğe — I Asked the Yellow Flower
note: By Yunus Emre (13th c.). A dialogue between the dervish and a fading yellow flower; each verse closes on the refrain of tawḥīd.

verses.ar:
Sordum sarı çiçeğe
Annen baban var mıdır?
Çiçek eydür derviş baba
Annem babam topraktır
Hak Lâ ilâhe illallah · Allah Lâ ilâhe illallah
verses.en: I asked the yellow flower: have you a mother and father? The flower said, 'Dervish father, my mother and father are the earth.' Truth — there is no god but Allah; Allah — there is no god but Allah.

verses.ar:
Sordum sarı çiçeğe
Sen kimin ümmetisin?
Çiçek eydür derviş baba
Muhammed ümmetiyim
Hak Lâ ilâhe illallah · Allah Lâ ilâhe illallah
verses.en: I asked the yellow flower: whose community are you of? The flower said, 'Dervish father, I am of Muhammad's community.' Truth — there is no god but Allah; Allah — there is no god but Allah.

verses.ar:
Sordum sarı çiçeğe
Evlat kardeş var mıdır?
Çiçek eydür derviş baba
Evlat kardeş yapraktır
Hak Lâ ilâhe illallah · Allah Lâ ilâhe illallah
verses.en: I asked the yellow flower: have you children and siblings? The flower said, 'Dervish father, my children and siblings are the leaves.' Truth — there is no god but Allah; Allah — there is no god but Allah.

verses.ar:
Sordum sarı çiçeğe
Niçin benzin sarıdır?
Çiçek eydür derviş baba
Ölüm bize yakındır
Hak Lâ ilâhe illallah · Allah Lâ ilâhe illallah
verses.en: I asked the yellow flower: why is your face so pale? The flower said, 'Dervish father, death is near to us.' Truth — there is no god but Allah; Allah — there is no god but Allah.

verses.ar:
Sordum sarı çiçeğe
Sen beni bilir misin?
Çiçek eydür derviş baba
Sen Yunus değil misin?
Hak Lâ ilâhe illallah · Allah Lâ ilâhe illallah
verses.en: I asked the yellow flower: do you know me? The flower said, 'Dervish father, are you not Yunus?' Truth — there is no god but Allah; Allah — there is no god but Allah.

titleEnglish: Dolap Niçin İnilersin — Dertli Dolap (The Sorrowful Waterwheel)
note: By Yunus Emre (13th c.). The water-wheel speaks: the felled tree that groans in longing for its Lord.

verses.ar:
Dolap niçin inilersin
Derdim vardır inilerim
Ben Mevlâ'ya âşık oldum
Anın için inilerim
verses.en: O waterwheel, why do you groan? I have a sorrow, so I groan. I have fallen in love with my Lord; for His sake I groan.

verses.ar:
Benim adım dertli dolap
Suyum akar yalap yalap
Böyle emreylemiş Çalap
Derdim vardır inilerim
verses.en: My name is the sorrowful wheel; my water flows glinting and gleaming. So has God ordained; I have a sorrow, so I groan.

verses.ar:
Beni bir dağda buldular
Kolum kanadım yoldular
Dolaba lâyık gördüler
Derdim vardır inilerim
verses.en: They found me upon a mountain; they tore away my arms and wings; they deemed me fit to be a wheel. I have a sorrow, so I groan.

verses.ar:
Ben bir dağın ağacıyım
Ne tatlıyım ne acıyım
Ben Mevlâ'ya duacıyım
Derdim vardır inilerim
verses.en: I am a tree of the mountain; I am neither sweet nor bitter. I am one who prays to my Lord. I have a sorrow, so I groan.

verses.ar:
Dağdan kestiler hezenim
Bozuldu türlü düzenim
Ben bir usanmaz ozanım
Derdim vardır inilerim
verses.en: They cut my great beams from the mountain; all my order was undone. I am a minstrel who never tires. I have a sorrow, so I groan.

verses.ar:
Şu dülgerler beni yondu
Her azam yerine kondu
Bu iniltim Hak'tan geldi
Derdim vardır inilerim
verses.en: These carpenters carved me; each of my limbs was set in its place. This groaning of mine came from the Truth. I have a sorrow, so I groan.

verses.ar:
Suyum alçaktan çekerim
Dönüp yükseğe dökerim
Görün ben neler çekerim
Derdim vardır inilerim
verses.en: I draw my water from below, and turning, pour it out on high. See what I endure! I have a sorrow, so I groan.

verses.ar:
Yunus burda gelen gülmez
Kişi muradına ermez
Bu fânide kimse kalmaz
Derdim vardır inilerim
verses.en: Yunus: none who comes here laughs; no one attains their heart's desire; no one remains in this passing world. I have a sorrow, so I groan.

titleEnglish: İlim İlim Bilmektir — Knowledge Is to Know
note: By Yunus Emre (13th c.). True knowledge is self-knowledge and knowing God — worth more than a thousand pilgrimages.

verses.ar:
İlim ilim bilmektir
İlim kendin bilmektir
Sen kendini bilmezsin
Ya nice okumaktır
verses.en: Knowledge is to know knowledge; knowledge is to know your own self. If you do not know yourself, then what is all this reading for?

verses.ar:
Okumaktan mana ne
Kişi Hakk'ı bilmektir
Çün okudun bilmezsin
Ha bir kuru emektir
verses.en: What is the meaning of reading? It is for one to know the Truth. If you have read yet still do not know, it is but dry, empty toil.

verses.ar:
Okudum bildim deme
Çok tâat kıldım deme
Eğer Hak bilmez isen
Abes yere yelmektir
verses.en: Do not say 'I have read and I know'; do not say 'I have worshipped much.' If you do not know the Truth, it is only running about in vain.

verses.ar:
Dört kitabın mânâsı
Bellidir bir elifte
Sen elifi bilmezsin
Bu nice okumaktır
verses.en: The meaning of the four Books is made plain in a single Alif. You do not know even the Alif — so what is all this reading?

verses.ar:
Yunus Emre der hoca
Gerekse bin var hacca
Hepisinden iyice
Bir gönüle girmektir
verses.en: Yunus Emre says: O teacher, though you go a thousand times to the Hajj — better than all of it is to enter and win a single heart.

titleEnglish: Adı Güzel Kendi Güzel Muhammed — Beautiful of Name, Beautiful of Self
note: A beloved naʿt attributed to Yunus Emre (13th c.), in praise of the Prophet ﷺ.

verses.ar:
Canım kurban olsun senin yoluna
Adı güzel kendi güzel Muhammed
Şefâat eyle bu kemter kuluna
Adı güzel kendi güzel Muhammed
verses.en: May my life be a sacrifice on your path — Muhammad, beautiful of name, beautiful of self. Intercede for this lowly servant — Muhammad, beautiful of name, beautiful of self.

verses.ar:
Mü'min olanların çoktur cefâsı
Ahirette olur zevk ü sefâsı
On sekiz bin âlemin Mustafâ'sı
Adı güzel kendi güzel Muhammed
verses.en: Those who believe bear much hardship; their joy and ease will come in the Hereafter. The Chosen One of the eighteen thousand worlds — Muhammad, beautiful of name, beautiful of self.

verses.ar:
Yedi kat gökleri seyrân eyleyen
Kürsü'nün üstünde cevlân eyleyen
Mi'racda ümmetini dileyen
Adı güzel kendi güzel Muhammed
verses.en: He who journeyed through the seven heavens, who moved above the Divine Footstool, who on the Ascension pleaded for his community — Muhammad, beautiful of name, beautiful of self.

verses.ar:
Ol çâryâr anın gökçek yâridir
Anı seven günahlardan beridir
On sekiz bin âlemin serveridir
Adı güzel kendi güzel Muhammed
verses.en: The four rightly-guided companions are his fair friends; whoever loves him is freed of sins. He is the master of the eighteen thousand worlds — Muhammad, beautiful of name, beautiful of self.

verses.ar:
Âşık Yunus neyler iki cihânı sensiz
Sen hak Peygambersin şeksiz şüphesiz
Sana uymayanlar gider imansız
Adı güzel kendi güzel Muhammed
verses.en: What would Yunus the lover do with both worlds without you? You are the true Prophet, beyond doubt or question. Those who do not follow you depart without faith — Muhammad, beautiful of name, beautiful of self.

titleEnglish: Derman Arardım Derdime — I Sought a Cure for My Ailment
note: By Niyazi Mısrî (17th c.). A classic of Sufi realization: the cure, the proof, and the Beloved were within all along.

verses.ar:
Derman arardım derdime
Derdim bana derman imiş
Bürhan sorardım aslıma
Aslım bana bürhan imiş
verses.en: I sought a cure for my ailment — my ailment itself was my cure. I sought a proof of my origin — my origin itself was my proof.

verses.ar:
Sağ u solum gözler idim
Dost yüzünü görsem deyu
Ben taşrada arar idim
Ol can içinde can imiş
verses.en: I searched to my right and left, longing to see the Friend's face; I was seeking outside, yet He was the very soul within the soul.

verses.ar:
Öyle sanırdım ayriyem
Dost gayridir ben gayriyem
Benden görüp işiteni
Bildim ki ol cânân imiş
verses.en: I used to think I was apart — that the Friend was other and I was other; then I knew that the One who sees and hears through me is the Beloved.

verses.ar:
Savm u salât u hac ile
Sanma biter zâhid işin
İnsan-ı kâmil olmaya
Lâzım olan irfan imiş
verses.en: Do not imagine, O ascetic, that your work is finished with fasting, prayer, and pilgrimage; what is needed to become a perfected human being is inner gnosis.

verses.ar:
Mürşid gerektir bildire
Hakk'ı sana Hakka'l-yakîn
Mürşidi olmayanların
Bildikleri gümân imiş
verses.en: A guide is needed to make you know the Truth with the certainty of direct knowledge; what those without a guide know is mere conjecture.

verses.ar:
Anla hemen bir sözdürür
Yokuş değildir düzdürür
Âlem kamu bir yüzdürür
Gören anı hayran imiş
verses.en: Understand at once: it is a single word, no steep climb but level ground; all the world is one single face — whoever sees it is lost in wonder.

verses.ar:
İşit Niyazi'nin sözün
Bir nesne örtmez Hak yüzün
Hak'tan ayan bir nesne yok
Gözsüzlere pinhan imiş
verses.en: Hear the word of Niyazi: nothing veils the face of the Truth; nothing is more manifest than the Truth — yet to the sightless it stays hidden.

titleEnglish: Dağlar İle Taşlar İle — Let Me Call Upon You, My Lord
note: By Yunus Emre (13th c.). With all of creation — mountains, birds, prophets — the poet calls upon his Lord.

verses.ar:
Dağlar ile taşlar ile
Çağırayım Mevlâm seni
Seherlerde kuşlar ile
Çağırayım Mevlâm seni
verses.en: With the mountains and the stones, let me call upon You, my Lord; with the birds at daybreak, let me call upon You, my Lord.

verses.ar:
Sular dibinde mâhi ile
Sahralarda âhu ile
Abdal olup yâhu ile
Çağırayım Mevlâm seni
verses.en: With the fish in the depths of the waters, with the gazelle upon the open plains, becoming a wandering dervish crying 'Yā Hū' — let me call upon You, my Lord.

verses.ar:
Gökyüzünde İsa ile
Tur dağında Musa ile
Elimdeki asâ ile
Çağırayım Mevlâm seni
verses.en: With Jesus in the heavens, with Moses on Mount Tur, with the staff in my hand — let me call upon You, my Lord.

verses.ar:
Derdi öküş Eyyub ile
Gözü yaşlı Yakub ile
Ol Muhammed mahbub ile
Çağırayım Mevlâm seni
verses.en: With sorely-afflicted Job, with tearful-eyed Jacob, with Muhammad the beloved — let me call upon You, my Lord.

verses.ar:
Hamd ü şükrullah ile
Vasf-ı Kulhüvallah ile
Dâima zikrullah ile
Çağırayım Mevlâm seni
verses.en: With praise and thanks to Allah, with the words 'Say: He is Allah,' always with the remembrance of Allah — let me call upon You, my Lord.

verses.ar:
Bilmişim dünya hâlini
Terk ettim kıyl ü kâlini
Baş açık ayak yalını
Çağırayım Mevlâm seni
verses.en: I have come to know the ways of this world; I have left its idle talk behind. Bare-headed and barefoot, let me call upon You, my Lord.

verses.ar:
Yunus okur diller ile
Ol kumru bülbüller ile
Hakk'ı seven kullar ile
Çağırayım Mevlâm seni
verses.en: Yunus recites with many tongues, with the doves and the nightingales, with the servants who love the Truth — let me call upon You, my Lord.

titleEnglish: Arayı Arayı Bulsam İzini — O Muhammad, My Soul Longs for You
note: A beloved naʿt in the tradition of Yunus Emre (13th c.), yearning for the Prophet ﷺ and his city.

verses.ar:
Arayı arayı bulsam izini
İzinin tozuna sürsem yüzümü
Hak nasip eylese görsem yüzünü
Ya Muhammed canım arzular seni
verses.en: If only, searching and searching, I could find his track and press my face into the dust of his footprints; if God would grant that I might see his face — O Muhammad, my soul longs for you.

verses.ar:
Bir mübarek sefer olsa da gitsem
Kâbe yollarında kumlara batsam
Hûb cemâlin bir kez düşte seyretsem
Ya Muhammed canım arzular seni
verses.en: If only there were a blessed journey and I could go, sinking into the sands on the roads to the Kaaba; if I could gaze upon your lovely face just once, even in a dream — O Muhammad, my soul longs for you.

verses.ar:
Zerrece kalmadı kalbimde hile
Sıtk ile girmişim ben hak yola
Ebû Bekir, Ömer, Osman'da bile
Ya Muhammed canım arzular seni
verses.en: Not a speck of guile remains in my heart; I have entered the true path in sincerity — alongside Abu Bakr, Umar, and Uthman — O Muhammad, my soul longs for you.

verses.ar:
Ali ile Hasan Hüseyin anda
Sevgisi gönülde muhabbeti canda
Yarın mahşer günü ulu divanda
Ya Muhammed canım arzular seni
verses.en: With Ali, and with Hasan and Husayn there — their love in the heart, their affection in the soul — tomorrow on the Day of Gathering, in the great assembly — O Muhammad, my soul longs for you.

verses.ar:
Arafat dağıdır bizim dağımız
Anda kabul olur bizim duamız
Medine'de yatar Peygamberimiz
Ya Muhammed canım arzular seni
verses.en: Mount Arafat is our mountain; there our prayers are answered; in Medina rests our Prophet — O Muhammad, my soul longs for you.
